Section 1: Quick Problems

Question 1

6 points
Compute u⋅v\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}u⋅v for u=⟨4,−1,2⟩\mathbf{u}=\langle 4,-1,2\rangleu=⟨4,−1,2⟩, v=⟨1,3,5⟩\mathbf{v}=\langle 1,3,5\ranglev=⟨1,3,5⟩.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Multiply Matching Components

    Multiply the first components together, then the second, then the third: 4⋅1=44 \cdot 1 = 44⋅1=4, (−1)⋅3=−3(-1) \cdot 3 = -3(−1)⋅3=−3 and 2⋅5=102 \cdot 5 = 102⋅5=10.

  2. Step 2: Add the Products

    u⋅v=4−3+10=11.\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v} = 4 - 3 + 10 = 11.u⋅v=4−3+10=11. The dot product is a single number, not a vector.

Answer

u⋅v=11\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v} = 11u⋅v=11

Question 2

6 points
Find a unit vector orthogonal to both ⟨2,1,0⟩\langle 2,1,0\rangle⟨2,1,0⟩ and ⟨0,1,3⟩\langle 0,1,3\rangle⟨0,1,3⟩. Compute the cross product and normalize.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Set Up the Cross Product

    The cross product of two vectors is orthogonal to both of them. Write it as a determinant:
    ⟨2,1,0⟩×⟨0,1,3⟩=∣ijk210013∣.\langle 2,1,0\rangle \times \langle 0,1,3\rangle = \begin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \end{vmatrix}.⟨2,1,0⟩×⟨0,1,3⟩=​i20​j11​k03​​.
    ⟨2,1,0⟩×⟨0,1,3⟩=∣ijk210013∣.\begin{aligned}& \langle 2,1,0\rangle \times \langle 0,1,3\rangle \\ &= \begin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}​⟨2,1,0⟩×⟨0,1,3⟩=​i20​j11​k03​​.​

  2. Step 2: Expand the Determinant

    i(1⋅3−0⋅1)−j(2⋅3−0⋅0)+k(2⋅1−1⋅0)=⟨3,−6,2⟩.\mathbf{i}(1 \cdot 3 - 0 \cdot 1) - \mathbf{j}(2 \cdot 3 - 0 \cdot 0) + \mathbf{k}(2 \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot 0) = \langle 3, -6, 2\rangle.i(1⋅3−0⋅1)−j(2⋅3−0⋅0)+k(2⋅1−1⋅0)=⟨3,−6,2⟩.
    i(1⋅3−0⋅1)−j(2⋅3−0⋅0)+k(2⋅1−1⋅0)=⟨3,−6,2⟩.\begin{aligned}& \mathbf{i}(1 \cdot 3 - 0 \cdot 1) \\ &\quad - \mathbf{j}(2 \cdot 3 - 0 \cdot 0) \\ &\quad + \mathbf{k}(2 \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot 0) \\ &= \langle 3, -6, 2\rangle.\end{aligned}​i(1⋅3−0⋅1)−j(2⋅3−0⋅0)+k(2⋅1−1⋅0)=⟨3,−6,2⟩.​
    Watch the minus sign on the j\mathbf{j}j term.

  3. Step 3: Check Orthogonality

    ⟨3,−6,2⟩⋅⟨2,1,0⟩=6−6+0=0\langle 3,-6,2\rangle \cdot \langle 2,1,0\rangle = 6 - 6 + 0 = 0⟨3,−6,2⟩⋅⟨2,1,0⟩=6−6+0=0 and ⟨3,−6,2⟩⋅⟨0,1,3⟩=0−6+6=0,\langle 3,-6,2\rangle \cdot \langle 0,1,3\rangle = 0 - 6 + 6 = 0,⟨3,−6,2⟩⋅⟨0,1,3⟩=0−6+6=0, so the cross product is orthogonal to both vectors.

  4. Step 4: Normalize

    The length is 9+36+4=49=7\sqrt{9 + 36 + 4} = \sqrt{49} = 79+36+4​=49​=7. Divide by the length to get ⟨37,−67,27⟩.\left\langle \tfrac37, -\tfrac67, \tfrac27 \right\rangle.⟨73​,−76​,72​⟩. Its negative is also a correct answer.

Answer

±17⟨3,−6,2⟩\pm\tfrac17\langle 3,-6,2\rangle±71​⟨3,−6,2⟩

Question 3

6 points
Find the equation ax+by+cz=dax + by + cz = dax+by+cz=d of the plane through (1,3,−2)(1,3,-2)(1,3,−2) with normal ⟨2,−1,3⟩\langle 2,-1,3\rangle⟨2,−1,3⟩.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Write the Point-Normal Form

    A plane through (x0,y0,z0)(x_0, y_0, z_0)(x0​,y0​,z0​) with normal ⟨a,b,c⟩\langle a, b, c\rangle⟨a,b,c⟩ is
    a(x−x0)+b(y−y0)+c(z−z0)=0.a(x - x_0) + b(y - y_0) + c(z - z_0) = 0.a(x−x0​)+b(y−y0​)+c(z−z0​)=0.
    Here that is
    2(x−1)−(y−3)+3(z+2)=0.2(x - 1) - (y - 3) + 3(z + 2) = 0.2(x−1)−(y−3)+3(z+2)=0.

  2. Step 2: Expand and Collect

    2x−2−y+3+3z+6=02x - 2 - y + 3 + 3z + 6 = 02x−2−y+3+3z+6=0, so 2x−y+3z=−72x - y + 3z = -72x−y+3z=−7.

  3. Step 3: Check the Point

    Substitute (1,3,−2)(1, 3, -2)(1,3,−2): 2(1)−3+3(−2)=−72(1) - 3 + 3(-2) = -72(1)−3+3(−2)=−7. The point lies on the plane.

Answer

2x−y+3z=−72x - y + 3z = -72x−y+3z=−7

Question 4

6 points
Find the curvature of the circle r(t)=⟨3cos⁡t,3sin⁡t,0⟩.\mathbf{r}(t) = \langle 3\cos t, 3\sin t, 0\rangle.r(t)=⟨3cost,3sint,0⟩.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Recall the Formula

    κ=∣r′(t)×r′′(t)∣∣r′(t)∣3\kappa = \frac{|\mathbf{r}'(t) \times \mathbf{r}''(t)|}{|\mathbf{r}'(t)|^3}κ=∣r′(t)∣3∣r′(t)×r′′(t)∣​
    κ=∣r′(t)×r′′(t)∣∣r′(t)∣3\begin{aligned}\kappa &= \frac{|\mathbf{r}'(t) \times \mathbf{r}''(t)|}{|\mathbf{r}'(t)|^3}\end{aligned}κ​=∣r′(t)∣3∣r′(t)×r′′(t)∣​​

  2. Step 2: Differentiate Twice

    r′(t)=⟨−3sin⁡t,3cos⁡t,0⟩\mathbf{r}'(t) = \langle -3\sin t, 3\cos t, 0\rangler′(t)=⟨−3sint,3cost,0⟩ and r′′(t)=⟨−3cos⁡t,−3sin⁡t,0⟩.\mathbf{r}''(t) = \langle -3\cos t, -3\sin t, 0\rangle.r′′(t)=⟨−3cost,−3sint,0⟩.

  3. Step 3: Compute the Cross Product

    Both vectors lie in the xyxyxy-plane, so only the k\mathbf{k}k component survives: (−3sin⁡t)(−3sin⁡t)−(3cos⁡t)(−3cos⁡t)=9sin⁡2t+9cos⁡2t=9.(-3\sin t)(-3\sin t) - (3\cos t)(-3\cos t) = 9\sin^2 t + 9\cos^2 t = 9.(−3sint)(−3sint)−(3cost)(−3cost)=9sin2t+9cos2t=9. So ∣r′×r′′∣=9|\mathbf{r}' \times \mathbf{r}''| = 9∣r′×r′′∣=9.

  4. Step 4: Compute the Speed

    ∣r′(t)∣=9sin⁡2t+9cos⁡2t=3,|\mathbf{r}'(t)| = \sqrt{9\sin^2 t + 9\cos^2 t} = 3,∣r′(t)∣=9sin2t+9cos2t​=3, so ∣r′(t)∣3=27|\mathbf{r}'(t)|^3 = 27∣r′(t)∣3=27.

  5. Step 5: Divide

    κ=927=13\kappa = \tfrac{9}{27} = \tfrac13κ=279​=31​. This matches the fact that a circle of radius RRR has curvature 1/R1/R1/R.

Answer

κ=13\kappa = \tfrac13κ=31​

Question 5

6 points
Compute ∫r′(t) dt\int \mathbf{r}'(t)\,dt∫r′(t)dt for r′(t)=⟨4t, 5, cos⁡t⟩.\mathbf{r}'(t) = \langle 4t,\allowbreak\, 5,\allowbreak\, \cos t\rangle.r′(t)=⟨4t,5,cost⟩. Integrate componentwise.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Integrate Each Component

    ∫4t dt=2t2+C1\int 4t\,dt = 2t^2 + C_1∫4tdt=2t2+C1​, ∫5 dt=5t+C2\int 5\,dt = 5t + C_2∫5dt=5t+C2​ and ∫cos⁡t dt=sin⁡t+C3\int \cos t\,dt = \sin t + C_3∫costdt=sint+C3​.

  2. Step 2: Collect the Constants

    The three constants form one constant vector C=⟨C1,C2,C3⟩.\mathbf{C} = \langle C_1, C_2, C_3\rangle.C=⟨C1​,C2​,C3​⟩. Check the result by differentiating each component: you get ⟨4t,5,cos⁡t⟩\langle 4t, 5, \cos t\rangle⟨4t,5,cost⟩ back.

Answer

⟨2t2, 5t, sin⁡t⟩+C,\langle 2t^2,\allowbreak\, 5t,\allowbreak\, \sin t\rangle + \mathbf{C},⟨2t2,5t,sint⟩+C, where C\mathbf{C}C is a constant vector

Question 6

6 points
Find the directional derivative of f(x,y)=xy2f(x,y) = x y^2f(x,y)=xy2 at (2,1)(2, 1)(2,1) in the direction ⟨3,4⟩\langle 3, 4\rangle⟨3,4⟩.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Find the Gradient

    ∇f=⟨fx,fy⟩=⟨y2, 2xy⟩.\nabla f = \langle f_x, f_y \rangle = \langle y^2,\allowbreak\, 2xy \rangle.∇f=⟨fx​,fy​⟩=⟨y2,2xy⟩.

  2. Step 2: Evaluate at the Point

    At (2,1)(2, 1)(2,1), ∇f=⟨1,4⟩\nabla f = \langle 1, 4 \rangle∇f=⟨1,4⟩.

  3. Step 3: Make the Direction a Unit Vector

    The formula needs a unit vector. ∣⟨3,4⟩∣=5|\langle 3, 4\rangle| = 5∣⟨3,4⟩∣=5, so u=⟨35,45⟩.\mathbf{u} = \left\langle \tfrac35, \tfrac45 \right\rangle.u=⟨53​,54​⟩.

  4. Step 4: Take the Dot Product

    Duf=∇f⋅u=1⋅35+4⋅45=195.D_{\mathbf{u}}f = \nabla f \cdot \mathbf{u} = 1 \cdot \tfrac35 + 4 \cdot \tfrac45 = \tfrac{19}{5}.Du​f=∇f⋅u=1⋅53​+4⋅54​=519​.

Answer

Duf(2,1)=195=3.8D_{\mathbf{u}}f(2,1) = \tfrac{19}{5} = 3.8Du​f(2,1)=519​=3.8

Question 7

6 points
Find fxyf_{xy}fxy​ for f(x,y)=x3eyf(x,y) = x^3 e^yf(x,y)=x3ey at (1,0)(1, 0)(1,0).
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Differentiate in xxx

    Treat yyy as a constant: fx=3x2eyf_x = 3x^2 e^yfx​=3x2ey.

  2. Step 2: Differentiate the Result in yyy

    Now treat xxx as a constant: fxy=(fx)y=3x2eyf_{xy} = (f_x)_y = 3x^2 e^yfxy​=(fx​)y​=3x2ey.

  3. Step 3: Evaluate at the Point

    At (1,0)(1, 0)(1,0), fxy=3⋅1⋅e0=3f_{xy} = 3 \cdot 1 \cdot e^0 = 3fxy​=3⋅1⋅e0=3. As a check, fy=x3eyf_y = x^3 e^yfy​=x3ey and fyx=3x2eyf_{yx} = 3x^2 e^yfyx​=3x2ey, the same function, as Clairaut's Theorem predicts.

Answer

fxy(1,0)=3f_{xy}(1, 0) = 3fxy​(1,0)=3

Question 8

6 points
Classify the critical point of f(x,y)=x2−xy+2y2−7yf(x,y) = x^2 - xy + 2y^2 - 7yf(x,y)=x2−xy+2y2−7y. Find the critical point and apply the second-derivative test.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Set the First Partials to Zero

    fx=2x−y=0f_x = 2x - y = 0fx​=2x−y=0 and fy=−x+4y−7=0f_y = -x + 4y - 7 = 0fy​=−x+4y−7=0.

  2. Step 2: Solve the System

    The first equation gives y=2xy = 2xy=2x. Substitute into the second: −x+8x−7=0-x + 8x - 7 = 0−x+8x−7=0, so x=1x = 1x=1 and y=2y = 2y=2. The critical point is (1,2)(1, 2)(1,2).

  3. Step 3: Compute the Second Partials

    fxx=2f_{xx} = 2fxx​=2, fyy=4f_{yy} = 4fyy​=4 and fxy=−1f_{xy} = -1fxy​=−1.

  4. Step 4: Apply the Test

    D=fxxfyy−(fxy)2=8−1=7.D = f_{xx}f_{yy} - (f_{xy})^2 = 8 - 1 = 7.D=fxx​fyy​−(fxy​)2=8−1=7. Since D>0D > 0D>0 and fxx>0f_{xx} > 0fxx​>0, the critical point is a local minimum. The minimum value is f(1,2)=1−2+8−14=−7f(1, 2) = 1 - 2 + 8 - 14 = -7f(1,2)=1−2+8−14=−7.

Answer

Local minimum at (1,2)(1, 2)(1,2), with f(1,2)=−7f(1,2) = -7f(1,2)=−7

Question 10

6 points
Set up (do not evaluate) a polar double integral for the area inside r=4cos⁡θr = 4\cos\thetar=4cosθ. Write the full integral with bounds and integrand.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Identify the Curve

    Multiply both sides by rrr: r2=4rcos⁡θr^2 = 4r\cos\thetar2=4rcosθ, which is x2+y2=4xx^2 + y^2 = 4xx2+y2=4x, or (x−2)2+y2=4(x - 2)^2 + y^2 = 4(x−2)2+y2=4. The curve is a circle of radius 2 centered at (2,0)(2, 0)(2,0), to the right of the yyy-axis.

  2. Step 2: Find the θ\thetaθ Range

    The radius 4cos⁡θ4\cos\theta4cosθ is positive when −π/2<θ<π/2-\pi/2 < \theta < \pi/2−π/2<θ<π/2, and this range traces the circle exactly once. Using 0≤θ≤2π0 \le \theta \le 2\pi0≤θ≤2π would trace it twice and double the area.

  3. Step 3: Write the Area Element

    Area is ∬D1 dA\iint_D 1\,dA∬D​1dA, and in polar coordinates dA=r dr dθdA = r\,dr\,d\thetadA=rdrdθ. For each θ\thetaθ, rrr runs from the origin out to the circle.

  4. Step 4: Assemble the Integral

    ∫−π/2π/2∫04cos⁡θr dr dθ\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\int_0^{4\cos\theta} r\,dr\,d\theta∫−π/2π/2​∫04cosθ​rdrdθ
    For reference, the integral equals 4π4\pi4π, the area of a circle of radius 2. The problem asks only for the set-up.

Answer

∫−π/2π/2∫04cos⁡θr dr dθ\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\int_0^{4\cos\theta} r\,dr\,d\theta∫−π/2π/2​∫04cosθ​rdrdθ

Question 12

6 points
Determine whether F(x,y)=⟨2x+3y, x+2y⟩\mathbf{F}(x,y) = \langle 2x + 3y,\allowbreak\, x + 2y\rangleF(x,y)=⟨2x+3y,x+2y⟩ is conservative.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Name PPP and QQQ

    P=2x+3yP = 2x + 3yP=2x+3y and Q=x+2yQ = x + 2yQ=x+2y.

  2. Step 2: Apply the Cross-Partials Test

    A vector field on all of R2\mathbb{R}^2R2 with continuous partial derivatives is conservative exactly when Py=QxP_y = Q_xPy​=Qx​. Here Py=3P_y = 3Py​=3 and Qx=1Q_x = 1Qx​=1.

  3. Step 3: Conclude

    Since 3≠13 \neq 13=1, F\mathbf{F}F is not conservative. You can also see this by trying to build a potential: ϕx=2x+3y\phi_x = 2x + 3yϕx​=2x+3y gives ϕ=x2+3xy+g(y)\phi = x^2 + 3xy + g(y)ϕ=x2+3xy+g(y), so ϕy=3x+g′(y)\phi_y = 3x + g'(y)ϕy​=3x+g′(y), which can never equal x+2yx + 2yx+2y.

Answer

Not conservative, because Py=3≠1=QxP_y = 3 \neq 1 = Q_xPy​=3=1=Qx​.

Answer

Question 15

6 points
True or False: If a simple closed curve CCC bounding a region DDD in the plane is traversed clockwise, then ∮CP dx+Q dy=−∬D(Qx−Py) dA.\displaystyle\oint_C P\,dx + Q\,dy = -\iint_D (Q_x - P_y)\,dA.∮C​Pdx+Qdy=−∬D​(Qx​−Py​)dA. State true or false and justify briefly.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Decide

    True.

  2. Step 2: Recall the Hypothesis

    Green's Theorem says ∮CP dx+Q dy=∬D(Qx−Py) dA\displaystyle\oint_C P\,dx + Q\,dy = \iint_D (Q_x - P_y)\,dA∮C​Pdx+Qdy=∬D​(Qx​−Py​)dA when CCC is positively oriented, which means counterclockwise, with DDD on the left as you walk along CCC.

  3. Step 3: See What Reversing Does

    Traversing a curve in the opposite direction changes the sign of a line integral, while the double integral over DDD does not change. So for the clockwise orientation, the line integral equals the negative of the double integral.

  4. Step 4: Check With an Example

    Take P=0P = 0P=0 and Q=xQ = xQ=x on the unit circle, so Qx−Py=1Q_x - P_y = 1Qx​−Py​=1 and the double integral is the area, π\piπ. Counterclockwise, with x=cos⁡tx = \cos tx=cost and y=sin⁡ty = \sin ty=sint, ∮Cx dy=∫02πcos⁡2t dt=π.\oint_C x\,dy = \int_0^{2\pi}\cos^2 t\,dt = \pi.∮C​xdy=∫02π​cos2tdt=π. Clockwise, the line integral is −π-\pi−π, which is the negative of the double integral.

Answer

True. Green's Theorem in its standard form needs the counterclockwise (positive) orientation; traversing CCC clockwise flips the sign of the line integral.

Question 16

18 points
Use the chain rule to find dzdt\dfrac{dz}{dt}dtdz​ at t=π/4t = \pi/4t=π/4 if z=xy2z = x y^2z=xy2, x=cos⁡tx = \cos tx=cost, y=sin⁡ty = \sin ty=sint.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Write the Chain Rule

    zzz depends on ttt through both xxx and yyy, so
    dzdt=∂z∂xdxdt+∂z∂ydydt.\frac{dz}{dt} = \frac{\partial z}{\partial x}\frac{dx}{dt} + \frac{\partial z}{\partial y}\frac{dy}{dt}.dtdz​=∂x∂z​dtdx​+∂y∂z​dtdy​.
    dzdt=∂z∂xdxdt+∂z∂ydydt.\begin{aligned}\frac{dz}{dt} &= \frac{\partial z}{\partial x}\frac{dx}{dt} \\ &\qquad + \frac{\partial z}{\partial y}\frac{dy}{dt}.\end{aligned}dtdz​​=∂x∂z​dtdx​+∂y∂z​dtdy​.​

  2. Step 2: Find the Partial Derivatives

    ∂z∂x=y2\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial x} = y^2∂x∂z​=y2 and ∂z∂y=2xy\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial y} = 2xy∂y∂z​=2xy.

  3. Step 3: Differentiate xxx and yyy

    dxdt=−sin⁡t\dfrac{dx}{dt} = -\sin tdtdx​=−sint and dydt=cos⁡t\dfrac{dy}{dt} = \cos tdtdy​=cost.

  4. Step 4: Evaluate at t=π/4t = \pi/4t=π/4

    At t=π/4t = \pi/4t=π/4, x=y=22x = y = \tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}x=y=22​​, dxdt=−22\tfrac{dx}{dt} = -\tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}dtdx​=−22​​ and dydt=22\tfrac{dy}{dt} = \tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}dtdy​=22​​. The partials are y2=12y^2 = \tfrac12y2=21​ and 2xy=12xy = 12xy=1.

  5. Step 5: Combine

    dzdt=12(−22)+1(22)=−24+22=24.\frac{dz}{dt} = \frac12\left(-\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right) + 1\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right) = -\frac{\sqrt2}{4} + \frac{\sqrt2}{2} = \frac{\sqrt2}{4}.dtdz​=21​(−22​​)+1(22​​)=−42​​+22​​=42​​.
    dzdt=12(−22)+1(22)=−24+22=24.\begin{aligned}\frac{dz}{dt} &= \frac12\left(-\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right) \\ &\qquad + 1\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right) \\ &= -\frac{\sqrt2}{4} + \frac{\sqrt2}{2} \\ &= \frac{\sqrt2}{4}.\end{aligned}dtdz​​=21​(−22​​)+1(22​​)=−42​​+22​​=42​​.​

  6. Step 6: Check Directly

    Substitute first: z=cos⁡tsin⁡2tz = \cos t\sin^2 tz=costsin2t, so dzdt=−sin⁡3t+2sin⁡tcos⁡2t.\tfrac{dz}{dt} = -\sin^3 t + 2\sin t\cos^2 t.dtdz​=−sin3t+2sintcos2t. At t=π/4t = \pi/4t=π/4 this is −24+22=24.-\tfrac{\sqrt2}{4} + \tfrac{\sqrt2}{2} = \tfrac{\sqrt2}{4}.−42​​+22​​=42​​.

Answer

dzdt∣t=π/4=24≈0.354\dfrac{dz}{dt}\Big|_{t=\pi/4} = \dfrac{\sqrt2}{4} \approx 0.354dtdz​​t=π/4​=42​​≈0.354

Question 17

18 points
Find the equation of the tangent plane to f(x,y)=ln⁡(x2+3y2)f(x,y) = \ln(x^2 + 3y^2)f(x,y)=ln(x2+3y2) at (1,1)(1, 1)(1,1).
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Find the Height of the Surface

    f(1,1)=ln⁡(1+3)=ln⁡4f(1, 1) = \ln(1 + 3) = \ln 4f(1,1)=ln(1+3)=ln4, so the point of tangency is (1,1,ln⁡4)(1, 1, \ln 4)(1,1,ln4).

  2. Step 2: Find fxf_xfx​

    By the chain rule, fx=2xx2+3y2f_x = \dfrac{2x}{x^2 + 3y^2}fx​=x2+3y22x​. At (1,1)(1,1)(1,1), fx=24=12f_x = \tfrac24 = \tfrac12fx​=42​=21​.

  3. Step 3: Find fyf_yfy​

    Similarly, fy=6yx2+3y2f_y = \dfrac{6y}{x^2 + 3y^2}fy​=x2+3y26y​. At (1,1)(1,1)(1,1), fy=64=32f_y = \tfrac64 = \tfrac32fy​=46​=23​.

  4. Step 4: Write the Tangent Plane

    The tangent plane at (a,b)(a, b)(a,b) is z=f(a,b)+fx(a,b)(x−a)+fy(a,b)(y−b),z = f(a,b) + f_x(a,b)(x - a) + f_y(a,b)(y - b),z=f(a,b)+fx​(a,b)(x−a)+fy​(a,b)(y−b), so
    z=ln⁡4+12(x−1)+32(y−1).z = \ln 4 + \tfrac12(x - 1) + \tfrac32(y - 1).z=ln4+21​(x−1)+23​(y−1).

  5. Step 5: Simplify

    Collect the constants: z=12x+32y−2+ln⁡4≈0.5x+1.5y−0.614.z = \tfrac12 x + \tfrac32 y - 2 + \ln 4 \approx 0.5x + 1.5y - 0.614.z=21​x+23​y−2+ln4≈0.5x+1.5y−0.614.

Answer

z=ln⁡4+12(x−1)+32(y−1),z = \ln 4 + \tfrac12(x - 1) + \tfrac32(y - 1),z=ln4+21​(x−1)+23​(y−1), or z=12x+32y−2+ln⁡4z = \tfrac12 x + \tfrac32 y - 2 + \ln 4z=21​x+23​y−2+ln4

Question 18

18 points
Use Lagrange multipliers to find the extrema of f(x,y)=xyf(x,y) = xyf(x,y)=xy subject to x2+4y2=8x^2 + 4y^2 = 8x2+4y2=8.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Set Up the System

    Let g(x,y)=x2+4y2g(x,y) = x^2 + 4y^2g(x,y)=x2+4y2. Then ∇f=⟨y,x⟩\nabla f = \langle y, x\rangle∇f=⟨y,x⟩ and ∇g=⟨2x,8y⟩\nabla g = \langle 2x, 8y\rangle∇g=⟨2x,8y⟩. The equations ∇f=λ∇g\nabla f = \lambda\nabla g∇f=λ∇g and g=8g = 8g=8 are
    y=2λx,x=8λy,x2+4y2=8.y = 2\lambda x,\qquad x = 8\lambda y,\qquad x^2 + 4y^2 = 8.y=2λx,x=8λy,x2+4y2=8.
    y=2λxx=8λyx2+4y2=8.\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned}y &= 2\lambda x\end{aligned} \\[6pt] \begin{aligned} x &= 8\lambda y\end{aligned} \\[6pt] \begin{aligned} x^2 + 4y^2 &= 8.\end{aligned}\end{gathered}y​=2λx​x​=8λy​x2+4y2​=8.​​

  2. Step 2: Rule Out Zero

    Substitute x=8λyx = 8\lambda yx=8λy into the first equation: y=16λ2yy = 16\lambda^2 yy=16λ2y. If y=0y = 0y=0, then x=8λ⋅0=0x = 8\lambda \cdot 0 = 0x=8λ⋅0=0, and (0,0)(0,0)(0,0) is not on the ellipse. So y≠0y \neq 0y=0, and dividing by yyy gives λ2=116\lambda^2 = \tfrac{1}{16}λ2=161​, so λ=±14\lambda = \pm\tfrac14λ=±41​.

  3. Step 3: Find the Candidate Points

    If λ=14\lambda = \tfrac14λ=41​, then x=2yx = 2yx=2y, and the constraint becomes 4y2+4y2=84y^2 + 4y^2 = 84y2+4y2=8, so y=±1y = \pm 1y=±1. This gives (2,1)(2, 1)(2,1) and (−2,−1)(-2, -1)(−2,−1). If λ=−14\lambda = -\tfrac14λ=−41​, then x=−2yx = -2yx=−2y, which gives (−2,1)(-2, 1)(−2,1) and (2,−1)(2, -1)(2,−1).

  4. Step 4: Evaluate fff

    f(2,1)=f(−2,−1)=2f(2, 1) = f(-2, -1) = 2f(2,1)=f(−2,−1)=2 and f(−2,1)=f(2,−1)=−2f(-2, 1) = f(2, -1) = -2f(−2,1)=f(2,−1)=−2.

  5. Step 5: Classify

    The ellipse is closed and bounded, so fff has an absolute maximum and an absolute minimum on it, and both must be among the candidates. The maximum is 2 and the minimum is −2-2−2.

Answer

Maximum 222 at (2,1)(2, 1)(2,1) and (−2,−1)(-2, -1)(−2,−1); minimum −2-2−2 at (−2,1)(-2, 1)(−2,1) and (2,−1)(2, -1)(2,−1)

Question 20

18 points
Use Green's Theorem to evaluate ∮C(xy dx+x2 dy)\displaystyle\oint_C (xy\,dx + x^2\,dy)∮C​(xydx+x2dy) where CCC is the boundary of the triangle with vertices (0,0)(0,0)(0,0), (2,0)(2,0)(2,0), (0,2)(0,2)(0,2) traversed counterclockwise.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Name PPP and QQQ

    P=xyP = xyP=xy and Q=x2Q = x^2Q=x2. The curve is closed and counterclockwise, so Green's Theorem applies: ∮CP dx+Q dy=∬D(Qx−Py) dA.\displaystyle\oint_C P\,dx + Q\,dy = \iint_D (Q_x - P_y)\,dA.∮C​Pdx+Qdy=∬D​(Qx​−Py​)dA.

  2. Step 2: Compute Qx−PyQ_x - P_yQx​−Py​

    Qx=2xQ_x = 2xQx​=2x and Py=xP_y = xPy​=x, so Qx−Py=xQ_x - P_y = xQx​−Py​=x.

  3. Step 3: Describe the Region

    The hypotenuse runs from (2,0)(2,0)(2,0) to (0,2)(0,2)(0,2) along the line x+y=2x + y = 2x+y=2. So DDD is 0≤x≤20 \le x \le 20≤x≤2, 0≤y≤2−x0 \le y \le 2 - x0≤y≤2−x.

  4. Step 4: Evaluate the Double Integral

    ∫02∫02−xx dy dx=∫02x(2−x) dx=[x2−x33]02=4−83=43.\int_0^2\int_0^{2-x} x\,dy\,dx = \int_0^2 x(2 - x)\,dx = \left[x^2 - \frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^2 = 4 - \frac83 = \frac43.∫02​∫02−x​xdydx=∫02​x(2−x)dx=[x2−3x3​]02​=4−38​=34​.
    ∫02∫02−xx dy dx=∫02x(2−x) dx=[x2−x33]02=4−83=43.\begin{aligned}& \int_0^2\int_0^{2-x} x\,dy\,dx \\ &= \int_0^2 x(2 - x)\,dx \\ &= \left[x^2 - \frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^2 \\ &= 4 - \frac83 \\ &= \frac43.\end{aligned}​∫02​∫02−x​xdydx=∫02​x(2−x)dx=[x2−3x3​]02​=4−38​=34​.​

  5. Step 5: Check Along the Edges

    On the bottom edge, y=0y = 0y=0 and dy=0dy = 0dy=0, so the integral is 0. On the left edge, x=0x = 0x=0, so P=Q=0P = Q = 0P=Q=0 and the integral is 0. On the hypotenuse, use x=2−tx = 2 - tx=2−t, y=ty = ty=t for 0≤t≤20 \le t \le 20≤t≤2, so dx=−dtdx = -dtdx=−dt and dy=dtdy = dtdy=dt:
    ∫02[−(2−t)t+(2−t)2]dt=∫02(4−6t+2t2) dt=8−12+163=43.\int_0^2 \left[-(2 - t)t + (2 - t)^2\right]dt = \int_0^2 (4 - 6t + 2t^2)\,dt = 8 - 12 + \frac{16}{3} = \frac43.∫02​[−(2−t)t+(2−t)2]dt=∫02​(4−6t+2t2)dt=8−12+316​=34​.
    ∫02[−(2−t)t+(2−t)2]dt=∫02(4−6t+2t2) dt=8−12+163=43.\begin{aligned}& \int_0^2 \left[-(2 - t)t + (2 - t)^2\right]dt \\ &= \int_0^2 (4 - 6t + 2t^2)\,dt \\ &= 8 - 12 + \frac{16}{3} \\ &= \frac43.\end{aligned}​∫02​[−(2−t)t+(2−t)2]dt=∫02​(4−6t+2t2)dt=8−12+316​=34​.​
    The edge total matches.

Answer

43\tfrac4334​

Question 21

Let QQQ be the solid bounded above by the sphere x2+y2+z2=18x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 18x2+y2+z2=18 and below by the cone z=x2+y2z = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}z=x2+y2​. Complete all four parts: (a) (7 pts) Sketch QQQ. Label the cone, the sphere and that circle.

    Combine these bounds with the volume element ρ2sin⁡ϕ dρ dϕ dθ\rho^2\sin\phi\,d\rho\,d\phi\,d\thetaρ2sinϕdρdϕdθ.
    V=∫02π∫0π/4∫032ρ2sin⁡ϕ dρ dϕ dθV = \int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{\pi/4}\int_0^{3\sqrt2} \rho^2\sin\phi\,d\rho\,d\phi\,d\thetaV=∫02π​∫0π/4​∫032​​ρ2sinϕdρdϕdθ
    V=∫02π∫0π/4∫032ρ2sin⁡ϕ dρ dϕ dθ\begin{aligned}V &= \int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{\pi/4}\int_0^{3\sqrt2} \rho^2\sin\phi\,d\rho\,d\phi\,d\theta\end{aligned}V​=∫02π​∫0π/4​∫032​​ρ2sinϕdρdϕdθ​

  5. Step 5: (c) Write the Cylindrical Integral

    For a fixed (r,θ)(r, \theta)(r,θ), zzz runs from the cone z=rz = rz=r up to the sphere z=18−r2z = \sqrt{18 - r^2}z=18−r2​. The shadow of the solid in the xyxyxy-plane is the disk r≤3r \le 3r≤3, the radius of the intersection circle, not the radius of the sphere.
    V=∫02π∫03∫r18−r2r dz dr dθV = \int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{3}\int_r^{\sqrt{18 - r^2}} r\,dz\,dr\,d\thetaV=∫02π​∫03​∫r18−r2​​rdzdrdθ
    V=∫02π∫03∫r18−r2r dz dr dθ\begin{aligned}V &= \int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{3}\int_r^{\sqrt{18 - r^2}} r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta\end{aligned}V​=∫02π​∫03​∫r18−r2​​rdzdrdθ​

    The integral separates into three factors: ∫02πdθ=2π\int_0^{2\pi} d\theta = 2\pi∫02π​dθ=2π, ∫0π/4sin⁡ϕ dϕ=1−22\int_0^{\pi/4}\sin\phi\,d\phi = 1 - \tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}∫0π/4​sinϕdϕ=1−22​​ and ∫032ρ2 dρ=(32)33=182.\int_0^{3\sqrt2}\rho^2\,d\rho = \tfrac{(3\sqrt2)^3}{3} = 18\sqrt2.∫032​​ρ2dρ=3(32​)3​=182​. Multiply them:
    V=2π(1−22)182=362 π−36π=36π(2−1).V = 2\pi\left(1 - \frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)18\sqrt2 = 36\sqrt2\,\pi - 36\pi = 36\pi(\sqrt2 - 1).V=2π(1−22​​)182​=362​π−36π=36π(2​−1).
    V=2π(1−22)182=362 π−36π=36π(2−1).\begin{aligned}V &= 2\pi\left(1 - \frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)18\sqrt2 \\ &= 36\sqrt2\,\pi - 36\pi \\ &= 36\pi(\sqrt2 - 1).\end{aligned}V​=2π(1−22​​)182​=362​π−36π=36π(2​−1).​

Question 22

44 points
Let F(x,y)=⟨2xy+2,  x2+sin⁡y⟩\mathbf{F}(x,y) = \langle 2xy + 2,\; x^2 + \sin y\rangleF(x,y)=⟨2xy+2,x2+siny⟩ and let CCC be the path from (0,0)(0, 0)(0,0) to (1,π)(1, \pi)(1,π) along y=πx2y = \pi x^2y=πx2. Complete all four parts: (a) (8 pts) Test whether F\mathbf{F}F is conservative. (b) (12 pts) If conservative, find a potential function. (c) (12 pts) Use the FTC for line integrals to evaluate ∫CF⋅dr\int_C \mathbf{F}\cdot d\mathbf{r}∫C​F⋅dr. (d) (12 pts) Verify by parameterizing CCC and computing directly.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: (a) Compare the Cross Partials

    P=2xy+2P = 2xy + 2P=2xy+2 and Q=x2+sin⁡yQ = x^2 + \sin yQ=x2+siny, so Py=2xP_y = 2xPy​=2x and Qx=2xQ_x = 2xQx​=2x. They are equal on all of R2\mathbb{R}^2R2, which has no holes, so F\mathbf{F}F is conservative.

  2. Step 2: (b) Integrate PPP in xxx

    A potential ϕ\phiϕ must satisfy ϕx=P\phi_x = Pϕx​=P. Integrate in xxx and leave room for a function of yyy: ϕ=x2y+2x+g(y)\phi = x^2 y + 2x + g(y)ϕ=x2y+2x+g(y).

  3. Step 3: (b) Match QQQ

    Differentiate in yyy: ϕy=x2+g′(y)\phi_y = x^2 + g'(y)ϕy​=x2+g′(y). This must equal x2+sin⁡yx^2 + \sin yx2+siny, so g′(y)=sin⁡yg'(y) = \sin yg′(y)=siny and g(y)=−cos⁡yg(y) = -\cos yg(y)=−cosy. The potential is
    ϕ(x,y)=x2y+2x−cos⁡y.\phi(x, y) = x^2 y + 2x - \cos y.ϕ(x,y)=x2y+2x−cosy.

  4. Step 4: (c) Apply the Fundamental Theorem

    For a conservative field, ∫C∇ϕ⋅dr=ϕ(end)−ϕ(start).\int_C \nabla\phi\cdot d\mathbf{r} = \phi(\text{end}) - \phi(\text{start}).∫C​∇ϕ⋅dr=ϕ(end)−ϕ(start). Here ϕ(1,π)=π+2−cos⁡π=π+3\phi(1, \pi) = \pi + 2 - \cos\pi = \pi + 3ϕ(1,π)=π+2−cosπ=π+3 and ϕ(0,0)=−cos⁡0=−1\phi(0, 0) = -\cos 0 = -1ϕ(0,0)=−cos0=−1, so the integral is (π+3)−(−1)=π+4(\pi + 3) - (-1) = \pi + 4(π+3)−(−1)=π+4.

    Let x=tx = tx=t and y=πt2y = \pi t^2y=πt2 for 0≤t≤10 \le t \le 10≤t≤1. Then dx=dtdx = dtdx=dt and dy=2πt dtdy = 2\pi t\,dtdy=2πtdt.

  6. Step 6: (d) Build the Integrand

    Substitute into P dx+Q dyP\,dx + Q\,dyPdx+Qdy:
    (2πt3+2)+(t2+sin⁡(πt2))2πt=4πt3+2+2πtsin⁡(πt2).\left(2\pi t^3 + 2\right) + \left(t^2 + \sin(\pi t^2)\right)2\pi t = 4\pi t^3 + 2 + 2\pi t\sin(\pi t^2).(2πt3+2)+(t2+sin(πt2))2πt=4πt3+2+2πtsin(πt2).
    (2πt3+2)+(t2+sin⁡(πt2))2πt=4πt3+2+2πtsin⁡(πt2).\begin{aligned}& \left(2\pi t^3 + 2\right) \\ &\quad + \left(t^2 + \sin(\pi t^2)\right)2\pi t \\ &= 4\pi t^3 + 2 + 2\pi t\sin(\pi t^2).\end{aligned}​(2πt3+2)+(t2+sin(πt2))2πt=4πt3+2+2πtsin(πt2).​

  7. Step 7: (d) Integrate

    ∫01(4πt3+2) dt=π+2\int_0^1 (4\pi t^3 + 2)\,dt = \pi + 2∫01​(4πt3+2)dt=π+2. For the last term, substitute u=πt2u = \pi t^2u=πt2, so du=2πt dtdu = 2\pi t\,dtdu=2πtdt and ∫012πtsin⁡(πt2) dt=∫0πsin⁡u du=2.\int_0^1 2\pi t\sin(\pi t^2)\,dt = \int_0^{\pi}\sin u\,du = 2.∫01​2πtsin(πt2)dt=∫0π​sinudu=2. The total is π+4\pi + 4π+4, which matches part (c).

(a) Conservative; (b) ϕ=x2y+2x−cos⁡y\phi = x^2 y + 2x - \cos yϕ=x2y+2x−cosy; (c) and (d) π+4≈7.142\pi + 4 \approx 7.142π+4≈7.142

Question 24

40 points
A vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨x2/2,  xy,  z2+1⟩\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \langle x^2/2,\; xy,\; z^2 + 1\rangleF(x,y,z)=⟨x2/2,xy,z2+1⟩ acts on a closed solid QQQ bounded above by the paraboloid z=9−x2−y2z = 9 - x^2 - y^2z=9−x2−y2 and below by the plane z=0z = 0z=0. (c) (14 pts) Use the Divergence Theorem to set up and evaluate the outward flux of F\mathbf{F}F across ∂Q\partial Q∂Q. Convert to cylindrical coordinates.   1. Step 1: (a) Sketch the Solid

    ∫02π∫03∫09−r2(2rcos⁡θ+2z) r dz dr dθ.\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^3\int_0^{9 - r^2} (2r\cos\theta + 2z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta.∫02π​∫03​∫09−r2​(2rcosθ+2z)rdzdrdθ.

  4. Step 4: (c) Evaluate

    The xxx-term integrates to 0 because ∫02πcos⁡θ dθ=0\int_0^{2\pi}\cos\theta\,d\theta = 0∫02π​cosθdθ=0; the solid is symmetric about the yzyzyz-plane. For the zzz-term, ∫09−r22z dz=(9−r2)2\int_0^{9 - r^2} 2z\,dz = (9 - r^2)^2∫09−r2​2zdz=(9−r2)2, so
    2π∫03(9−r2)2 r dr=2π[−(9−r2)36]03=2π⋅7296=243π.2\pi\int_0^3 (9 - r^2)^2\,r\,dr = 2\pi\left[-\frac{(9 - r^2)^3}{6}\right]_0^3 = 2\pi \cdot \frac{729}{6} = 243\pi.2π∫03​(9−r2)2rdr=2π[−6(9−r2)3​]03​=2π⋅6729​=243π.
    2π∫03(9−r2)2 r dr=2π[−(9−r2)36]03=2π⋅7296=243π.\begin{aligned}& 2\pi\int_0^3 (9 - r^2)^2\,r\,dr \\ &= 2\pi\left[-\frac{(9 - r^2)^3}{6}\right]_0^3 \\ &= 2\pi \cdot \frac{729}{6} \\ &= 243\pi.\end{aligned}​2π∫03​(9−r2)2rdr=2π[−6(9−r2)3​]03​=2π⋅6729​=243π.​
